subject.title: feat: version field in health response + POST /admin/update endpoint

question: Should OpenClaw expose update execution to gateway-authenticated HTTP callers, and if so should it be through the existing opt-in Admin HTTP RPC plugin or a dedicated `/admin/update` endpoint?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats `update.run` as an admin control-plane write and keeps it out of the Admin HTTP RPC allowlist, so exposing it over HTTP changes the network-accessible host update boundary.

options.title: Split and defer HTTP update authority
options.body: Keep the health-version discussion on the canonical version issue and require maintainer-owned security/API design before exposing update execution over HTTP.

options.title: Expose through Admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Allow or wrap `update.run` in the opt-in plugin only with explicit private-ingress, auth, audit, rate-limit, target-version, and handoff-failure requirements.

options.title: Reject HTTP update execution
options.body: Keep update execution limited to existing CLI/WebSocket/control-plane surfaces and document that fleet tools should use those or an external orchestrator.

recommendation.title: Split and defer HTTP update authority
recommendation.body: Keep the health-version discussion on the canonical version issue and require maintainer-owned security/API design before exposing update execution over HTTP.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history signal across the update-run control-plane path and adjacent version/admin surfaces.
